root_cause.text: In `drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c:smi_work()`, the sender-error path failed to clear `intf->curr_msg` and dispose of `newmsg`, leaving the same IPMI message/reply object to be retried and its `recv_msg` re-queued, causing double list insertion and subsequent use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that after `sender()` fails, "`intf->curr_msg` is not cleared" and "`newmsg` still points to the message," so a second failure calls `deliver_err_response()` on "the same `recv_msg` that was already queued for delivery"; the patch fixes this by setting `intf->curr_msg = NULL`, calling `ipmi_free_smi_msg(newmsg)`, and `newmsg = NULL` before `goto restart`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear `intf->curr_msg` under the proper lock before freeing the failed message to avoid leaving a stale current-message pointer on restart.
intent_record.what: The change replaces the previous conditional that only freed `newmsg` when `newmsg->recv_msg` was absent with a new sequence that, after optionally delivering an error response, conditionally takes `intf->xmit_msgs_lock` when not in run-to-completion mode, sets `intf->curr_msg = NULL`, releases the lock if taken, frees `newmsg` unconditionally, sets `newmsg = NULL`, and then jumps to `restart`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the current transmit message pointer is cleared before restarting after this error path, while properly synchronizing that update when needed. It prevents `intf->curr_msg` from continuing to reference a message that has just been freed, avoiding stale state and potential use-after-free or message-handling corruption on subsequent processing.

That leaves a stale current-message pointer so the same message/reply object can be retried, causing its recv_msg to be re-queued and leading to double list insertion and eventual use-after-free.

This error-response call is part of the sender-error path that disposes of or re-queues state associated with newmsg->recv_msg while intf->curr_msg still points at the same in-flight object. Because the stale current-message pointer is not cleared before continuing, the same recv_msg can later be processed again, contributing to double enqueue and use-after-free.
